mcqs.question: Which of the following objects is a magnet?
mcqs.explanation: Steel is a ferromagnetic material, meaning it can be magnetized and will be attracted to a magnet. Wood, plastic, and glass are non‑magnetic, so they will not behave like a magnet.

mcqs.question: To test whether a material is magnetic, a student should:

options.A: Place the material near a known magnet and see if it is attracted
options.B: Heat the material and observe any colour change
options.C: Submerge it in water and see if it floats
options.D: Rub it with a cloth to see if it becomes shiny

mcqs.answer: Place the material near a known magnet and see if it is attracted
mcqs.explanation: Magnetic behaviour is identified by attraction or repulsion with a known magnet. Heating, floating, or polishing do not reveal magnetic properties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a magnetic material?

options.A: A material that can be magnetized and attracts iron
options.B: A material that conducts electricity well
options.D: A material that is heavier than water

mcqs.answer: A material that can be magnetized and attracts iron
mcqs.explanation: Magnetic materials (like iron, nickel, cobalt) can become magnetized and will attract other magnetic objects. Conductivity, transparency, and density are unrelated properties.

mcqs.question: A student wants to separate non‑magnetic items from magnetic ones using a magnet. Which item will NOT be attracted?
mcqs.explanation: Aluminum is a non‑ferromagnetic metal, so it is not attracted to a magnet. Iron, steel, and nickel are magnetic and will be pulled toward the magnet.

mcqs.learning_point: Understanding attraction between a magnet and a magnetic material
mcqs.question: When a bar magnet is placed near a paperclip, what happens?

options.A: The paperclip is repelled away from the magnet
options.B: The paperclip is attracted and sticks to the magnet
options.C: There is no effect because paperclips are non‑magnetic
options.D: The magnet loses its strength immediately

mcqs.answer: The paperclip is attracted and sticks to the magnet
mcqs.explanation: Paperclips are made of steel, a magnetic material, so they are attracted to a magnet and will cling to it. Repulsion does not occur between a magnet and a magnetic material of the same polarity, and the magnet does not lose strength by attracting a paperclip.

mcqs.question: You find a rectangular bar in a drawer and want to know if it is a magnet. Which method will correctly tell you?

options.A: Hang it from a string and see if it aligns north‑south
options.B: Bring a compass near it; if the needle deflects, it is a magnet
options.C: Drop it; if it bounces higher, it is a magnet
options.D: Heat it; if it glows, it is a magnet

mcqs.answer: Bring a compass near it; if the needle deflects, it is a magnet
mcqs.explanation: A magnet creates a magnetic field that will cause a nearby compass needle to move. Hanging a bar does not reveal magnetism, and bouncing or glowing are unrelated phenomena.

mcqs.question: Which statement about metals and magnets is correct?

options.A: All metals are attracted to magnets
options.B: Only ferromagnetic metals like iron, nickel, and cobalt are attracted to magnets
options.C: Metals become magnetic when placed near a magnet
options.D: Plastic can be magnetic if it is painted with metallic paint

mcqs.answer: Only ferromagnetic metals like iron, nickel, and cobalt are attracted to magnets
mcqs.explanation: Only certain metals (ferromagnetic) show strong attraction to magnets. Other metals such as copper, aluminum, and gold are not attracted. Metals do not become magnetic merely by proximity, and plastic cannot become magnetic by painting.

mcqs.question: Which group of items contains only magnetic materials?

options.A: Iron nail, copper wire, plastic bottle
options.B: Nickel coin, steel spoon, aluminum foil
options.C: Iron nail, steel paperclip, nickel coin
options.D: Glass jar, wooden block, rubber eraser

mcqs.answer: Iron nail, steel paperclip, nickel coin
mcqs.explanation: Iron, steel, and nickel are all ferromagnetic and are attracted to magnets. Copper and aluminum are non‑magnetic, and glass, wood, and rubber are also non‑magnetic.
